parts.text: Which claim best explains why holding the breath soon becomes difficult?

options.text: The body needs oxygen from the air we breathe, so holding the breath cannot continue for long.
The body needs nitrogen from the air, so holding the breath soon fails.
The body stops all of its functions the instant Dev holds his breath.
Humans die within a few minutes without food or water, which is why he surfaces.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Dev tries to swim a few strokes underwater in the school pool without breathing. After a short time he has to come up for air.

part_answers.answer: Breathing brings oxygen the body needs. Without a fresh supply, breath-holding quickly becomes difficult; nitrogen, instant total shutdown, or lack of food/water are not the reason he surfaces so soon.

teacher.key_rationale: Air we breathe supplies oxygen the body needs, so breath-holding soon becomes difficult. The need is oxygen, not nitrogen; functions do not stop instantly; and food or water last far longer than a few minutes.
